verdict: Adequate for the current HSConfig no-block proof goal: the 11 representative decks plus supplemental CuteWarrior are broad enough to show that valid Wild deck inputs can still produce load-safe packages without requiring every mechanic family to be fully lowered.
source_backed_evidence: docs/operator/archetype-fixture-matrix.json defines an 11-row representative matrix: ShadowPriest, CtAPaladin, PirateRogue, BigShaman, Discolock, TreantDruid, ImbueMage, MechPala, Kingslayer, Boarlock, and PirateDH.

docs/operator/supplemental-proof-decks.json keeps CuteWarrior as supplemental_load_safe_prepare_proof and explicitly says it does not widen the representative matrix unless a future review proves a real missing family.

tests/test_universal_wild_no_block_matrix.py runs all 12 target decks through prepare and requires status=passed, technical_status=VALID_PACKAGE, runtime_load_safe=true, runtime_apply_mode=load_safe_apply, GlobalValues.json, Mulligan.json, and one per-card JSON file for every unique deck CardID.
tests/test_supplemental_cute_warrior_load_safe.py separately proves CuteWarrior remains load-safe on the prepare path even while staying supplemental.

docs/operator/universal-wild-no-block-contract.md states that load-safe apply is the runtime promise, that warning-only mechanics do not block a valid package, and that per-card-every-card coverage is HSConfig rich-output policy rather than the minimal runtime-apply gate.

The focused proof suite passed on 2026-07-10: python -m pytest tests/test_universal_wild_no_block_matrix.py tests/test_source_informed_closure_contract.py tests/test_matrix_governance.py tests/test_output_competence_matrix.py tests/test_matrix_current_truth.py -q, with 36 passed in 19.40s.
repo_observations: The matrix is intentionally split into 9 core_source_backed_fixture rows and 2 source_informed_valid_fixture rows. The two source-informed controls are Kingslayer and Boarlock, and both still produce VALID_PACKAGE plus load_safe_apply while keeping their source-depth gaps visible.

CuteWarrior is part of the universal no-block proof set but not part of the representative matrix. That preserves a lean representative count while still covering the low-curve Warrior acceptance lane.

The target deck list spans the main shell families that matter for load-safe pre-run packaging: aggro burn and hero-power transform via ShadowPriest; recruit and board flood via CtAPaladin; pirate weapon tempo via PirateRogue; big recruit and deathrattle cheat via BigShaman; discard and hand mutation via Discolock; token board snowball via TreantDruid; hero-power and spell-generation pressure via ImbueMage; mech and magnetic scaling via MechPala; weapon sequence pressure via Kingslayer; combo control with Combo.json via Boarlock; pirate hero-attack pressure via PirateDH; and low-curve Warrior via CuteWarrior.
The current contract treats weaker mechanics and weaker source depth as warning visibility, not as package blockers, as long as the emitted runtime shape remains structurally valid.

The active docs explicitly warn against widening the matrix just to add more deck names. New representative rows are supposed to be justified by a proven missing family, not by overlap with families that are already covered.
no_block_implications: This deck set is strong enough for the stated goal because it exercises the main package-shape lanes that can fail before runtime: exact deck identity, per-card JSON emission, required GlobalValues and Mulligan surfaces, optional Combo.json only where a combo shell needs it, and valid-package behavior even when source depth is incomplete.

Keeping Kingslayer and Boarlock in the matrix is important to the no-block claim. They prove that source-informed or partially blocked semantic depth can still remain warning-visible while the package stays load-safe and apply-allowed.
Keeping CuteWarrior supplemental is also appropriate for the no-block claim. It adds a narrow acceptance proof without distorting the representative matrix into a popularity list.

The current matrix supports a bounded engineering claim: the current representative and supplemental set is adequate as a regression net for valid Wild deck inputs to stay load-safe even when some mechanics remain partial or warning-only.

The matrix does not need every mechanic to be first-class lowered to be useful. It only needs enough shell diversity to prove that unsupported or partial mechanics are suppressed honestly instead of turning valid packages into false hard blocks.
gaps_or_risks: The matrix is finite, so it is not a literal proof for every future Wild deck family or every future mechanic combination.

The current deck set does not isolate some beyond-scope families as primary representatives, especially secret-heavy or discover-chain-heavy pressure, overload-first timing, or location-heavy reactive control.

Kingslayer still has an exact Quick Pick mulligan closure gap, and Boarlock still has an exact Fracking mulligan closure gap plus source-informed blockers. Those are honest preserved limitations, not reasons to reject the current no-block proof.
If package-builder logic, apply-gate logic, or runtime-surface emission rules change materially, this adequacy judgment should be rechecked by rerunning the focused matrix suite.
recommended_next_action: Keep the current 11 representative rows plus supplemental CuteWarrior unchanged, and rerun the focused 12-deck matrix proof suite whenever prepare, apply-gate, or runtime-surface logic changes.
